Has the legs to go and touch the cushions. Shahidi and Raza share a big smile on their faces as the post-match formalities follow

21:49 Local Time, 17:49 GMT, 23:19 IST: Afghanistan the best side in this tri-series and they have won this final at their own pace. Plenty of Afghan support in the stands and they are all delighted. Evans and Ibrahim Zadran have a chat as they walk back. The former checking the bat of the latter. Zimbabwe like Bangladesh in the last game didn't get enough on the board to pose a threat in this game. The openers began well with Gurbaz showing aggressive intent. Once Zimbabwe didn't get early wickets, that was game done then. Even though they got two wickets in quick time, Rahmat Shah and Zadran shut the door to take their side home. Afghanistan were easily the best side in this tri-series and in these conditions both Bangladesh and Zimbabwe were no match to them. Stay tuned for the post-match stuff...

Gurbaz 5/5: [On what Rahmat Shah is like as a captain and whether he is as calm on the field as he appears] You can see from the camera screen, the way you can see outside, he's exactly the same in the ground. He's very calm, cool. He tries to communicate things. He tries to ask every single person in the squad. He's not someone that, oh, I am okay, no, I don't need anyone. He will try to come and take advantage from everyone's experience. So he's some of that guy. I mean, he's very calm, as you can see (with) his batting. As calm as he is in the batting, he's calm as a captain as well. So he's a legend, no doubt. He's such a calm guy and good cricketer as well.

Rashid Khan | Player of the Series (1/2): [On taking 11 wickets in three matches and winning another PoTS award in ODIs] And nothing much, just try my best to keep the consistency as I have and keep the hard work up and keep repeating my performance, and try my best to beat my last game performance. So I think that's something which always have the mentality and making sure I enjoy my game. That's something which is more important for me. [On carrying this momentum into the T20I series after Afghanistan's recent 3-0 series loss to India] Well, good morale for us as a team to go for the T20 series. We haven't had that great series against India and lots of learning from that. But for us, the challenge will be like how we as a team manage ourselves to perform well in T20s as well and to make sure we, those areas we were, like struggling against India, try to improve it day by day, game by game, and take this momentum to the T20s.

Sikandar Raza | Zimbabwe captain (1/3): [On Zimbabwe's defeat in the final and whether he felt let down by a lack of support from the other batters] No, I wouldn't say that it feels disappointing that I was left alone. Cricket is never about one guy. There was a lot of good things that was done from the other boys as well. But for me, as much you said congratulations for making the final, but that is not how we want to play the final. This business of us making the final needs to stop. We address that in the changing room, that once we get to the final, we have to win the final. We have to win the trophies. This Zimbabwe needs to change. We have made plenty of finals and just existed. And for me, the biggest disappointment of this tour has been that we've been 20 for 3 and 30 for 3, and that's something we have addressed. But unfortunately we haven't got it right in three games, and that's an area of concern.

Raza (3/3): [On Zimbabwe's prospects in the upcoming T20I and Test series against Afghanistan] Yeah, hopefully if we can get over the injuries that we have already. If everybody's fit, I feel like the T20 series and the Test series should be a better contested series than the ODI series against Afghanistan, because we would have been here for at least 10 days, and I think that would have given us enough time to acclimatise as well. So I'm very hopeful that the T20 series and the Test match will be a better series. But certainly the ODI series we found it tough, and unfortunately it didn't help that three or four of our boys have been injured.

Rahmat Shah | Afghanistan captain (translated from Pashto): [On winning the tri-series and what the victory means to Afghanistan] Congratulations to all our countrymen. It is certainly a matter of great pride that we have won this tri-series. [On the importance of rotating the strike and building the partnership without hitting boundaries for 98 deliveries] Our discussion was that we had to bat deep and rotate the strike. The more we rotate the strike, the more pressure we put on the opposition. That was one of the reasons. In a final, we didn't want to give our wickets away either. They were looking for wickets, so we didn't try too much to hit boundaries. We focused on rotating the strike. [On Afghanistan's winning run and becoming the first Afghan captain to record seven consecutive ODI victories] Whatever we have achieved, whether in batting or bowling, is the result of everyone's effort. That is why our winning percentage has also improved. God willing, we will try to maintain this momentum.

The winning trophy is presented to Rahmat who is all smiles. Then he takes it and gives it to Omarzai and the Afghanistan team pose in front of the champions hoarding. 3 little kids are there sitting on the ground - probably the children of the players or support staff. 7 wins in a row for Rahmat Shah to start his captaincy career and he is unbeaten still in this format.
